question_put_to_the_owner: A Gate 0 TERMINAL receipt exists (DBX_RECEIPT__S32_GATE0__AUTHORITY_REISSUE_COMPILATION_BLOCKED__20260802T1110CDT.json, Drive ID 1qwdfvWUGJiWmzEc6Ll4_BdD2z3kvcGwE, sentinel S32_AUTHORITY_REISSUE_COMPILATION_BLOCKED) although no START/CLAIM receipt ever preceded it, and the newer 00_OPERATOR_NEXT_ACTION__...__20260802T1118CDT record still asserts Gate 0 is unclaimed and unterminated. Does the 1110CDT record consume the sole command's single terminal slot?

RULING.plain_statement: The 1110CDT record is classified as a BLOCKED diagnostic record, not as the sole command's one terminal receipt. It sits in the same class as the 1043CDT and 1102CDT records.

basis_cited_to_the_owner: The 1110CDT record's own drive_control_snapshot.queue.claim_status is NOT_VALIDLY_ESTABLISHED, so its emitter agrees it never validly claimed the command.
Its own single_next_permitted_action speaks of establishing controls 'before any new Gate 0 attempt', which presupposes that a further Gate 0 attempt is legitimate.
The 1118CDT operator direction, authored after the record landed, treats Gate 0 as still claimable.
This reading requires no new command to be authored and preserves the sole-command rule intact.

CONSTRAINTS_PRESERVED_BY_THIS_RULING: This ruling does NOT authorize a Gate 0 claim. Claiming remains a separate deliberate step reserved to the authorized Windows Control Tower on the host that owns C:\DataBoss.

This ruling does NOT disarm the live unbound Section 32 Cursor worker PID 49548, which remains a live blocker.
This ruling does NOT retire, edit, delete, or diminish the 1110CDT record. That record is preserved unmodified at its published bytes and its substantive findings stand.
This ruling does NOT remove the HOLD and does NOT authorize external release.
